title.narrative: Enhancing Health Resilience for Drought Response and Emergency Support in Takhar Province

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtJohanniter International Assistance (JUH) has prepared for the activation of an anticipatory trigger to respond to a forecasted drought emergency. The aim is to reduce morbidity and mortality while improving the health resilience of drought-affected populations in selected remote areas of three isolated districts of Eshkamesh, Kalafgan, and Bangi in Takhar Province (designated as "white areas") with a catchment population of 89,090 individuals. These areas were jointly identified with local public health authorities. The actions aim to strengthen health resilience in the drought-affected districts of Takhar, and JUH remains flexible to shift assistance to other locations within the province as needed. In addition, health services in the Takhar Mobile Health Clinics will be made accessible and safe for women, girls—including adolescents—and marginalized groups through the presence of female health workers or gender focal points, the establishment of women-friendly and adolescent-inclusive spaces, GBV mitigation measures, safe access to health services, and the provision of culturally appropriate, equitable, and gender-responsive care tailored to the needs of all community members.ltbrgtDrought can rapidly escalate into a full-scale health emergency due to the scarcity of clean water for drinking, hygiene, and sanitation. Communities are often forced to rely on unsafe water sources, increasing the risk of waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid, and diarrhea. It also creates favorable conditions for the spread of vector-borne diseases. Additionally, drought leads to crop failure and livestock losses, contributing to food insecurity and malnutrition, particularly among children, whose weakened immune systems heighten vulnerability to disease and death.ltbrgtTo support the health system in addressing these challenges, while maintaining the flexibility to respond to potential disease outbreaks within target areas, JUH will rapidly implement anticipatory actions upon trigger activation. The response will focus on mitigating anticipated public health risks, particularly waterborne diseases, by expanding access to primary healthcare services through eight deployed Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs). These teams aim to promote best health practices and reduce morbidity and mortality from preventable illnesses. This project aims to expand access to outpatient services through mobile clinics, delivering integrated healthcare, including maternal health, mental health support, disease surveillance, and prevention. Nutrition-specific interventions will involve community-based screening for malnutrition and referral to existing Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFPs), along with referrals to inpatient stabilization centers for children with severe acute malnutrition and complications. These efforts aim to enhance early detection, effective management, and recovery from malnutrition while ensuring access to comprehensive inpatient care when necessary.ltbrgtThe project will deploy MHNTs to deliver treatment for common illnesses, including reproductive health issues, and conduct disease surveillance to detect and prevent outbreaks. Health education sessions will support disease prevention and early care-seeking behaviors, integrated with community-led initiatives like those by CHVs and Health Shuras. MHNTs will flexibly reach remote drought-affected areas, ensuring continuity of services with pre-positioned medical supplies. Their mobility enables timely response to emergencies. Data collection will support monitoring and adaptation. Prioritizing access, quality, and community engagement, the project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality and strengthen local health systems through integrated, survivor-centered, and resilient service delivery.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
